raw_response:
*Settling in on the edge of the kang after breakfast, thinking through the season ahead…*

---

Same as always, really. Twenty-six years I've farmed this land and it doesn't change much. Seven mu total — five mu I do wheat then maize, turn it right around after harvest, same field. Two mu cotton, always kept that side field in cotton because my wife and daughter can help pick in autumn when work in town is slow.

My son went to Shijiazhuang last year for factory work, so the cotton is the worry — picking is all hands. Two mu I can manage with the family. If I had more I'd be scrambling.

---

**Wheat (the five mu, October through June)**

I plant around Hanlu, early October, when the soil temperature feels right and the neighbors start going. I buy seed from the village co-op, the Jimai kind they sell there — same seed everyone around here uses. Never saved my own wheat seed, I've seen that go wrong.

Before plowing I broadcast one bag of that black-bag compound fertilizer per mu — the 45 or 50 jin bags. That goes under when the tractor comes to plow. Then in early March when the wheat comes back green after winter, I spread some urea on top — about half a bag per mu, maybe a little less if money is tight this year. Two times is all I do for fertilizer.

Irrigation I do three times. Once before I sow to wet the ground down if it's been dry — October can be dry. Again in March when it greens up. Again at heading time in late April or early May — if I skip that one and it doesn't rain, the grain fills badly and I lose 50-100 jin per mu. That's too much to risk. Three times is enough normally.

For weeds I spray herbicide once in winter — early December usually, before the wheat gets too big. If I see rust on the leaves in spring I'll spray something for that, but most years it's fine here.

I hire the tractor operator from the village for plowing and for sowing — he has the seeder attachment. I pay per mu. For harvest I call the combine in June, same man who does the whole village. I pay him and it's done in a day.

---

**Maize (same five mu, June through September)**

The rush is after wheat. I try to get maize in within three or four days of harvest — the combine leaves and I have to move fast. I hire the rotary tiller to chop the wheat stubble and I plant the same day or next day if possible.

I plant hybrid seed — costs more than wheat seed but the yield difference is real.郑单958 or whatever they're selling at the co-op this year, something like that. My neighbor across the road switched to a new variety last year and it yielded well — I might ask him what it was.

Same compound fertilizer at planting, one bag per mu. When the plants are knee-high, around July, I topdress urea again, maybe half a bag. That's it for fertilizer — can't afford more and I've seen neighbors go overboard with no benefit.

Summer maize I might irrigate once if July is dry, but usually the summer rains are okay. Last year I didn't irrigate at all and yield was fine. If it's very dry in August I'll irrigate before silking — that's the worst time to have drought.

Herbicide once right after planting, before the weeds come up. Maize is easier than wheat for weeds in my experience.

Combine harvest in late September. Quick.

---

**Cotton (the two mu, April through October)**

Cotton starts in April — I plow that field in spring and plant around Guyu (谷雨, around April 20). Hybrid cotton seed from the store. This crop I baby more because picking is all hand labor and cotton prices per jin have been reasonable.

I put down fertilizer three times: once before transplanting, once in July when it's flowering, once in August when the bolls are setting. I use less per application than wheat — cotton doesn't need as much nitrogen or the plant goes all to leaves.

I irrigate twice: once in June if it's dry before flowering, once in August if needed. Cotton doesn't like waterlogged roots so I'm careful not to over-irrigate.

Pesticide is the headache. Bollworm spray twice or three times in July and August — I watch for the egg patches on leaves and spray when I see them. Aphids early in the season, one spray usually handles it. Herbicide once at the start.

Picking starts in September and goes until October, three or four rounds. My wife and daughter do most of it on weekends. It takes a lot of days all together. If I had four or five mu of cotton I'd need to hire people, but two mu we manage.

---

The season's mapped out. Cotton is the gamble as always — if prices hold and the bollworm doesn't hit, those two mu will pay better per mu than wheat or maize. But wheat-maize is the backbone. That's what keeps the family fed and what I'll still be doing when I'm sixty.
